Sparse attention — patterns and selection

The most crowded area at the conference and mostly incremental. Three ideas were worth keeping: token permutation, low-bit estimation, and scoring with the value norm.

SALE : Low-bit Estimation for Efficient Sparse Attention in Long-context LLM Prefilling

Worth reading
ICML 2026 · https://openreview.net/pdf?id=WyGEJKjvJN

TL;DREstimate the attention map cheaply at 4/8-bit, then decide what to compute in full precision. ~3× prefill speedup at large scale with quality on par with full attention; needs offline calibration.

My notes
This is very interesting and VERY SIMILAR to Sparsefinder! I like it
Key idea 1: use 4 or 8-bit attention and then isnpect the attention map
Key idea 2: relative importance by comparinh with sink and local (end of seq) regions...
requires offline calibration
The rest is just trivial
Results with big models (nice). On par with full attention but roughly 3x speed up. Nice!
I think this work is interesting for accelerating prefill
TagJoão Neves · Gonçalo Duarte · Nuno Gonçalves

Sparser Block-Sparse Attention via Token Permutation

Mixed
ICML 2026 · https://openreview.net/pdf?id=5u3Ra6Qf5C

TL;DRPermute keys and values so that the active entries cluster into fewer blocks, making block-sparse prefill cheaper. The permutation idea is good; their importance estimator is not.

My notes
Focus on prefilling
Trivial theorems given that attention itself is permutation invariant (without positional encoding nor causal mask)
I liked the idea of permuting keys/values a lot as it can be quite useful for sparse attention. However, their method is so naive: use the last block of queries to estimate the importance scores for permutation (the literaly just compute some scores with that and do argsort...). I bet there are better alternatives here, especially if we already have some stats a priori like the max of QK_i or something like that
TagNuno Gonçalves · Tomás Simões · João Neves

Stem: Rethinking Causal Information Flow in Sparse Attention

Mixed
ICML 2026 · https://openreview.net/pdf?id=8WrMPCd7Kr

TL;DRTwo ideas: vary k across positions rather than fixing it, and score keys using the value norm ‖V‖ rather than the attention weight alone.

My notes
The novel idea 1 is to increase k from k_min to k_max in the first positions, keep uniform for some steps, and in the end decrease from k_max to k_min again...
Novel idea 2: use also ||V|| for scoring. That's nice and connects to a wide-range literature on interpretability of attention (e.g., "attention is not only a weight" paper)
The idea 2 is nice but in practice they just butcher the idea because they approximate Q and K... That also makes things harder bc we need to compute Q and K first and then include V too, which costs another reading from HBM.
TagNuno Gonçalves · Emmanouil Zaranis

Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference

Not useful
ICML 2026 · https://openreview.net/pdf?id=o3gN27ITWV

TL;DRHierarchical sparse attention with a learned boundary detector that decides where chunks start and end — but the detector is trained offline on materialised attention maps, and it is applied to existing softmax models at prefill only.

My notes
The idea is quite nice and related to Dash Attention.
Dynamic Boundary Detection: they use a binary classifier to determine when there's a boundary between two tokens. I'm not sure how this works and how important it is, but it's something that we were interested for the next versions of DashAttention (DA)
The bad part about the dynamic boundary detector is that it needs to be trained a priori based on attention maps. I don't like that because (1): it's not trained end-to-end (I hate having multiple architectural stages), (2) it's costly because retrieving attention heads is costly (requires materializing P), and (3) there's no guarantee that the boundary really helps in anything, especially when extrapolating to longer sequences
It's a method applied on top of already existing softmax models! So they do NOT train their method, which is silly. They apply only to prefill which is interesting in my opinion given what the guy from Together AI said about prefilling being more costly than generation
Results show small degratation (no improvements) over the base model
TagNuno Gonçalves

LoSA: Locality Aware Sparse Attention in Diffusion Language Models

Mixed
ICML 2026 · https://openreview.net/pdf?id=SMhHoUepeR

TL;DRSparse attention for diffusion LMs, where the absence of a causal mask lets you select a subset of queries as well as keys.

My notes
Attention for diffusion (basically without causal masking). They then go beyond related works and approximate attention by selecting a set of queries and set of keys (instead of just keys).
I think the method is naive but I found interesting that in these models we can also do something regarding queries too. Might be useful for tabular foundation models, thought I'm not completely sure

Decoding and speculative decoding

Newer than the training-side work, and the three mechanisms here compose rather than compete: exact-support decoding, a variable draft budget, and a variable emission length.

GPU kernels, numerics and optimal transport

Also very nice work.

Outside ICML, same window

Not from the conference, picked up on arXiv in the same period, and two of them are more consequential than most of the ICML list.

Lost in Backpropagation: The LM Head is a Gradient Bottleneck

Worth reading
COLM 2026 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10145

TL;DRThe softmax bottleneck is an optimization problem, not only an expressivity one: 95–99% of the logit-gradient norm is destroyed by the rank-D LM head, and a bigger D gives a ×16 convergence speedup at fixed backbone.

My notes
This paper (not from icml) is relevant for Hugo and Nuno's paper on sparse losses

Worth reading
arXiv 2026 (under review) · https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19660

TL;DRIdentifies Token Norm Imbalance as the bottleneck for per-channel KV quantization, and fixes it with rotation plus per-token scaling. Near-lossless INT2, 3.0× decoding over BF16 FlashDecoding-v2.

Worth reading
